subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: generates the quantum states of light used as qubits.

subsystems.name: Photonic processor
subsystems.role: a chip-scale mesh of interferometers that manipulates light to perform gates.

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: configures the chip and reads out measurement results.

subsystems.name: Error correction and encoding
subsystems.role: protects quantum information against loss and noise using bosonic codes.

buildSteps.title: Design the photonic circuit and error-correcting code
buildSteps.detail: Specify the interferometer mesh, the encoding (e.g. GKP states), and the measurement pattern for a given algorithm.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the photonic integrated circuit
buildSteps.detail: Use silicon photonics or similar: deposit and etch waveguides, beam splitters and phase shifters on a chip, aiming for very low optical loss.

buildSteps.title: Generate and prepare the light
buildSteps.detail: Produce squeezed light or single photons using nonlinear optics, either off-chip and coupled in, or integrated on-chip.

buildSteps.title: Integrate detectors
buildSteps.detail: Attach or fabricate single-photon detectors, often superconducting nanowires that need cooling to a few kelvin, and couple them to the chip outputs.

buildSteps.title: Package and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Align and bond fibres, tune phase shifters, and measure loss and fidelity of the optical circuit.

buildSteps.title: Operate the processor
buildSteps.detail: Use control electronics to set the circuit, inject light, and read out photon detections to obtain results.

buildSteps.title: Scale with error correction
buildSteps.detail: Combine many modules via optical interconnects and implement real-time feedback to correct errors, moving toward fault tolerance.

prerequisites.why: on-demand single photons and squeezed states exist but need higher efficiency and purity for scaling.
fabrication must achieve extremely low optical loss to preserve quantum states.
superconducting nanowire detectors are highly efficient but need cryogenic cooling; room-temperature alternatives are noisier.
encoding and real-time feedback at the required scale have not been demonstrated.
photonic chips can be made in CMOS foundries, but quantum-specific integration and packaging are not yet standard.

pathway.milestone: small-scale photonic processors demonstrating quantum advantage in specific tasks such as boson sampling
pathway.unlocks: validation of the approach and early applications in sampling.

pathway.milestone: programmable photonic quantum computers with tens to hundreds of modes and basic error detection
pathway.unlocks: early quantum algorithms and error-corrected logical qubits.

pathway.milestone: modular systems interconnected by optical fibre, with real-time error correction
pathway.unlocks: scaling to thousands of qubits and distributed quantum computing.
practical quantum simulation, optimisation and cryptography at scale.
